title: 2 Chronicles 8
paragraphs: ¹ At the end of twenty years, during which Solomon had built the house of the LORD and his own palace, ² Solomon rebuilt the towns that Huram had given him and settled Israelites in them. ³ He also went to Hamath-zobah and captured it. ⁴ He built up Tadmor in the wilderness and all the store cities in Hamath. ⁵ He rebuilt Upper Beth-horon and Lower Beth-horon — fortified cities with walls, gates, and bars —

⁶ as well as Baalath, all the store cities that belonged to Solomon, all the cities for his chariots and horses, and everything he wanted to build in Jerusalem, in Lebanon, and throughout all the land under his rule. ⁷ All the people left from the Hittites, Amorites, Perizzites, Hivites, and Jebusites — peoples who were not Israelites — ⁸ that is, their descendants who remained in the land after the Israelites had failed to destroy them — Solomon conscripted for forced labor, as it is to this day. ⁹ But Solomon did not make slaves of the Israelites for his work. They served as soldiers, commanders of his forces, and commanders of his chariots and cavalry. ¹⁰ These were King Solomon's chief overseers — two hundred and fifty of them — who supervised the workers.

¹¹ Solomon brought Pharaoh's daughter up from the city of David to the palace he had built for her, for he said, "My wife must not live in the palace of David king of Israel, since the places where the ark of the LORD has entered are holy." ¹² On the altar of the LORD that he had built in front of the portico, Solomon offered burnt offerings to the LORD, ¹³ following the daily schedule set by Moses, on the Sabbaths, at the new moon festivals, and at the three annual festivals — the Festival of Unleavened Bread, the Festival of Weeks, and the Festival of Tabernacles. ¹⁴ According to the order of his father David, he organized the divisions of the priests for their duties and the Levites for their responsibilities — to lead praise and to minister alongside the priests, as each day required — and the gatekeepers by their divisions at each gate, for this was what David the man of God had commanded. ¹⁵ They did not deviate from the king's commands to the priests and Levites on any matter, including the treasuries.

¹⁶ All of Solomon's work was carried out from the day the foundation of the LORD's temple was laid until it was completed. So the house of the LORD was finished. ¹⁷ Then Solomon went to Ezion-geber and Elath on the shore of the Red Sea in the land of Edom. ¹⁸ Huram sent him ships commanded by his own officers and crewed by experienced sailors. They sailed to Ophir with Solomon's servants and brought back four hundred and fifty talents of gold to King Solomon.
